opportunities.candidate: For a fixed finite-dimensional B, faithful sigma, and arbitrary raw two-output CPTP broadcaster B, one EB map depending only on (B,sigma) is proposed to satisfy e_Psi(rho)^3 <= [240(2+sqrt(2))/pi] I(R:B)_rho sqrt(b_B(rho)) simultaneously for all finite R and rho_B=sigma.
opportunities.candidate_validation: Not checked by this literature subtask; mathematical proof remains external to this report.
closest_prior: Barnum-Caves-Fuchs-Jozsa-Schumacher (1996): exact common-channel broadcasting of a state set iff its members commute; qualitative only.

Piani (2016), using finite-shareability/de Finetti results: a k-Bose-symmetric extendible channel has a common EB approximation uniformly over reference states with half trace error <= d/k; symmetric-support premise and dimension dependence remain.

Chiribella (2011): permutation-invariant M-output broadcasters admit common measure-and-prepare approximations to k-output restrictions with error <= 2 d^2 k/M; it is a many-output/dimension-dependent route.

Piani (2017) and Xie-Fang-Wang-Duan (2017): approximate local broadcasting is quantified by per-state or finite-prior average fidelity/discord objectives, without the proposed all-extension common EB trace estimate.
opportunities.precise_gap: A dimension- and reference-independent quantitative implication from small two-marginal identity error on every extension of one faithful marginal, with total mutual-information budget C, to one EB reconstruction map for the entire extension family.
opportunities.if_candidate_survives: A dimension-free quantitative stability theorem at the exact no-broadcast/classicality boundary, using two raw output marginals and uniform over all finite quantum references.
opportunities.priority: UNKNOWN; bounded search is not evidence of novelty.
